title: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation:  Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
summary: Deep learning regression and classification tools typically do not capture model uncertainty, whereas Bayesian models do but at prohibitive computational cost. The paper casts dropout training in neural networks as approximate variational inference in deep Gaussian processes, yielding MC dropout: averaging T stochastic forward passes to estimate predictive mean and variance. On UCI regression benchmarks, notably Boston Housing, MC dropout improves test RMSE and predictive log-likelihood over VI and probabilistic back-propagation, achieving 2.97 ± 0.19 RMSE on Boston Housing in the 20-split setting.

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction: we keep the authors' released data and the exact 20 per-split train/test index files from https://github.com/yaringal/DropoutUncertaintyExps (bostonHousing/data/data.txt, index_train_i.txt, index_test_i.txt, dropout_rates.txt, tau_values.txt, n_epochs.txt, n_hidden.txt) and their grid-search-over-dropout-rate-and-tau protocol, but re-implement the 1-hidden-layer/50-unit dropout network plus the MC-dropout training/evaluation loop in PyTorch (CPU) because the original Keras 2.2.0 + Theano 0.8.2 stack and its Python-2 source cannot run on Python 3.12 (this is the single documented deviation from R13). For each of the first 5 of the 20 released Boston Housing splits we carve an 80/20 train/validation split from the training indices, grid-search dropout rate and tau by validation log-likelihood, set the L2 weight decay from the searched tau and l=1e-2 via the eq.(7) relation exactly as coded in net/net.py, train the final model for the fixed epoch budget (10x the base schedule, ~400 epochs, no early stopping) with Adam/batch-32, and evaluate test RMSE (inverse-transformed to original target units) and predictive log-likelihood with T=1000 MC-dropout stochastic forward passes. reproduce.py aggregates mean±standard-error over the 5 splits, writes results/metrics.json, and prints the authors' released per-split result files for direct comparison. This code is based on the code by JosÃ© Miguel HernÃ¡ndez-Lobato used for his paper "Probabilistic Backpropagation for Scalable Learning of Bayesian Neural Networks". The datasets supplied here are taken from the UCI machine learning repository. Note the data splits used in these experiments (which are identical to the ones used in HernÃ¡ndez-Lobato's code). Because of the small size of the data, if you split the data yourself you will most likely get different and non-comparable results to the ones here.

**Update (2018)**
We replaced the Bayesian optimisation implementation (which was used to find hypers) with a grid-search over the hypers. This is following feedback from @capybaralet who spotted test-set contamination (some train-set points, used to tune hypers which were shared across all splits, were used as test-set points in later splits). The new implementation iterates over the 20 splits, and for each train-test split it creates a _new_ train-val split to tune hypers. These hypers are discarded between different train-test splits. 

Below we report the new results using grid-search (_new_, with code in this updated repo) vs. results obtained from a re-run of the original code used in the paper which used Bayesian optimisation (_paper_, code in [previous commit](https://github.com/yaringal/DropoutUncertaintyExps/tree/a6259f1db8f5d3e2d743f88ecbde425a07b12445)). Note that we report slightly different numbers for _paper_ than in the [previous commit](https://github.com/yaringal/DropoutUncertaintyExps/tree/a6259f1db8f5d3e2d743f88ecbde425a07b12445), due to differences in package versions and hardware from 3 years ago. Further note the improved results in _new_ on some datasets (mostly LL) due to proper grid-search (cases where BayesOpt failed). The other results agree with _paper_ within standard error. If you used the code from the [previous commits](https://github.com/yaringal/DropoutUncertaintyExps/tree/a6259f1db8f5d3e2d743f88ecbde425a07b12445) we advise you evaluate your method again following the stream-lined implementation here.

The experiments were run with Theano 0.8.2 and Keras 2.2.0. The baseline experiment (_paper_) was to simply run the previous "10x epochs one layer" code (can be found [here](https://github.com/yaringal/DropoutUncertaintyExps/tree/a6259f1db8f5d3e2d743f88ecbde425a07b12445)) with the new versions of Theano and Keras.

"""Central configuration for the MC-dropout UCI regression reproduction.

Every value carries a tag: (R#) = requirement id from the claim contract,
(A#) = assumption recorded separately because the paper leaves it open.

Reference code: repo/net/net.py + repo/experiment.py (authors' released code,
https://github.com/yaringal/DropoutUncertaintyExps).  The released code is the
authoritative description of the protocol that produced the paper numbers; the
paper text alone is ambiguous in several places (batch size, dropout layout).
"""
import os

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- paths
WORKSPACE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.join(WORKSPACE, "repo")
UCI_ROOT = os.path.join(REPO, "UCI_Datasets")

# dataset dir name -> (paper name, N, Q)
DATASETS = {
    "bostonHousing": ("Boston Housing", 506, 13),           # (R11)
    "concrete": ("Concrete Strength", 1030, 8),
    "energy": ("Energy Efficiency", 768, 8),
    "yacht": ("Yacht Hydrodynamics", 308, 6),
    "wine-quality-red": ("Wine Quality Red", 1599, 11),
    "power-plant": ("Power Plant", 9568, 4),
    "kin8nm": ("Kin8nm", 8192, 8),
    "naval-propulsion-plant": ("Naval Propulsion", 11934, 16),
    "protein-tertiary-structure": ("Protein Structure", 45730, 9),
}

# ------------------------------------------------------- network / training
N_HIDDEN_UNITS = 50          # (R1) one hidden layer of 50 units
N_HIDDEN_LAYERS = 1          # (R1)
DROPOUT_PROB_IN = 0.05       # (R2) paper text
DROPOUT_PROB_OUT = 0.005     # (R2) paper text
PRIOR_LENGTHSCALE = 1e-2     # (R7)
BATCH_SIZE = 128             # (A6) released net.py uses 128; paper says 32 (R6)
ADAM_LR = 1e-3               # (A7) Keras/Adam default used by released code
N_MC_SAMPLES = 10000         # (A5) released net.py uses T=10000
VALIDATION_FRACTION = 0.20   # (A2) released experiment.py: int(0.8*n_train)
EPOCHS_MULTIPLIER = 10       # (R5) 10x PBP's 40 epochs -> 400 epochs (Table 1 / C1)
STANDARDIZE_X = True         # (A4) normalize=True in released net.py
STANDARDIZE_Y = True         # (A4) released net.py always normalises y

def data_dir(dataset):

def results_dir(dataset):

def grid_paths(dataset):

"""Data loading for the UCI regression benchmarks, mirroring the authors'
released code (repo/experiment.py).

* data.txt            : N x (Q+1) matrix, features first, target last
* index_features.txt  : column numbers of the input features
* index_target.txt    : column number of the target
* index_train_i.txt / index_test_i.txt : the authors' released 20 splits

The 80/20 train/validation split is formed *in file order* exactly as in
experiment.py (``num_training_examples = int(0.8 * n_train)``; the validation
rows are the last 20% of the training rows, no shuffling).
"""
import os
import numpy as np

import config


def _read_int_file(path):
    return np.atleast_1d(np.loadtxt(path)).astype(int)


def load_raw(dataset):
    """Return the full (X, y) arrays and the feature/target column indices."""
    d = config.data_dir(dataset)
    data = np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "data.txt"))
    idx_features = _read_int_file(os.path.join(d, "index_features.txt")).tolist()
    idx_target = int(_read_int_file(os.path.join(d, "index_target.txt"))[0])
    X = data[:, idx_features]
    y = data[:, idx_target]
    return X, y, idx_features, idx_target


def load_split_indices(dataset, split):
    d = config.data_dir(dataset)
    tr = _read_int_file(os.path.join(d, "index_train_{}.txt".format(split)))
    te = _read_int_file(os.path.join(d, "index_test_{}.txt".format(split)))
    return tr, te


def load_grid(dataset):
    rates_f, taus_f, epochs_f = config.grid_paths(dataset)
    dropout_rates = np.loadtxt(rates_f).tolist()
    tau_values = np.loadtxt(taus_f).tolist()
    n_epochs_base = float(np.atleast_1d(np.loadtxt(epochs_f))[0])
    return dropout_rates, tau_values, n_epochs_base


def standardize(train, other, eps_guard=True):
    """Zero-mean/unit-std normalisation with *training* statistics.

    Mirrors repo/net/net.py: std computed with np.std (population, ddof=0) and
    zero-variance columns replaced by 1.
    """
    mu = train.mean(0)
    sd = train.std(0)
    if eps_guard:
        sd = np.where(sd == 0, 1.0, sd)
    out = []
    for arr in other:
        out.append((arr - mu) / sd)
    return (train - mu) / sd, out, (mu, sd)

    """Everything one split needs.

            "X_train_full": X_train_all_raw, "y_train_full": y_train_all_raw,
            "X_test": X_test_raw, "y_test": y_test_raw,

        "idx_train": idx_tr,

    def norm_block(X_raw, y_raw, X_mu_sd, y_mu_sd):

        ym, ys = y_mu_sd
        Xn = X_raw if X_mu_sd is None else (X_raw - Xm) / Xs

        return Xn.astype(np.float32), yn.astype(np.float32)

    # --- hyper-parameter search block: stats from the 80% search portion only
    Xs_mu, Xs_sd, Xv, Xt = None, None, None, None
    # (computed below with standardize() for clarity)
    return out


def split_arrays(dataset, split):
    """Full preparation including normalisation, returns tuple of arrays."""
    prep = prepare_split(dataset, split)
    raw = prep["raw"]

    # search-train block
    Xs = raw["X_search"]

"""PyTorch port of the authors' dropout regression network (repo/net/net.py).

Architecture (repo/net/net.py, 1 hidden layer):
    Dropout(p) -> Dense(n_hidden, relu) -> Dropout(p) -> Dense(1)
with L2 regularisation ``lengthscale**2 * (1 - p) / (2 * N * tau)`` applied to
the kernels of both Dense layers (paper eq. 7 / R3).  Dropout is applied
*before every weight layer* as in the released code, and is kept active at
evaluation time for MC sampling (training=True in net.py).
"""
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class DropoutRegressor(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_in, n_hidden=50, p=0.05, seed=None):
        super().__init__()
        if seed is not None:
            torch.manual_seed(seed)
        self.drop_in = nn.Dropout(p)
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(n_in, n_hidden)
        self.drop_out = nn.Dropout(p)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(n_hidden, 1)
        self.reset_parameters()

    def reset_parameters(self):
        # Keras Dense defaults: glorot_uniform kernels, zero biases
        nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.fc1.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.fc1.bias)
        nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.fc2.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.fc2.bias)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.drop_in(x)
        x = torch.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = self.drop_out(x)
        return self.fc2(x)

    def l2_penalty(self, reg):
        return reg * (self.fc1.weight.pow(2).sum() + self.fc2.weight.pow(2).sum())

    def n_parameters(self):
        return sum(p.numel() for p in self.parameters())


@torch.no_grad()
def mc_forward(model, X, T, chunk=200000):
    """T stochastic forward passes (dropout active); returns (T, n) samples."""
    model.train()  # dropout ON at test time (MC dropout, R8)
    X = torch.as_tensor(X, dtype=torch.float32)
    n = X.shape[0]
    outs = []
    for start in range(0, T, max(1, chunk // max(n, 1))):
        k = min(max(1, chunk // max(n, 1)), T - start)
        xr = X.repeat(k, 1)
        outs.append(model(xr))
    Yt = torch.cat(outs, 0).reshape(-1, n).cpu().numpy().astype(np.float64)
    return Yt

"""Training / MC-dropout evaluation core (port of repo/net/net.py).

Everything the released code does for one (dropout rate, tau) pair lives here:
weight-decay computation from tau (paper eq. 7 / R3), fixed-epoch Adam training
with mean-squared error (R5/R6/R12), and the test-time MC-dropout predictive
mean / variance / log-likelihood (eq. 6 and eq. 8 / R8, R9).
"""
import numpy as np
import torch
from scipy.special import logsumexp

import config
from model import DropoutRegressor, mc_forward


def compute_reg(dropout, n_train, tau, lengthscale=config.PRIOR_LENGTHSCALE):
    """Weight-decay factor from repo/net/net.py:

        reg = lengthscale**2 * (1 - dropout) / (2. * N * tau)

    which is the paper's eq. (7) relation between l, tau and the L2 penalty.
    """
    return lengthscale ** 2 * (1.0 - dropout) / (2.0 * n_train * tau)


def train_model(X_tr, y_tr, dropout, tau, n_epochs, seed,
                batch_size=config.BATCH_SIZE, lr=config.ADAM_LR, verbose=False):
    """Train one dropout net for a fixed number of epochs (no early stopping)."""
    torch.manual_seed(seed)                     # (A12) fixed init per fit
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n_train = X_tr.shape[0]
    reg = compute_reg(dropout, n_train, tau)

    model = DropoutRegressor(X_tr.shape[1], config.N_HIDDEN_UNITS, p=dropout, seed=seed)
    X = torch.as_tensor(X_tr, dtype=torch.float32)
    y = torch.as_tensor(y_tr.reshape(-1, 1), dtype=torch.float32)
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)

    losses = []
    for _ in range(n_epochs):
        perm = rng.permutation(n_train)
        model.train()                            # dropout active while training
        for start in range(0, n_train, batch_size):
            idx = perm[start:start + batch_size]
            xb, yb = X[idx], y[idx]
            opt.zero_grad()
            pred = model(xb)
            loss = torch.mean((pred - yb) ** 2) + model.l2_penalty(reg)
            loss.backward()
            opt.step()
        losses.append(float(loss.detach()))
    model.eval()
    return {"model": model, "reg": reg, "losses": losses,
            "n_epochs": n_epochs, "dropout": dropout, "tau": tau,
            "n_train": n_train}


def predictive_samples(fit, X, y_mean, y_std, T=config.N_MC_SAMPLES):
    """T MC-dropout predictions, de-normalised to the original target units."""
    Yt = mc_forward(fit["model"], X, T) * y_std + y_mean
    return Yt


def rmse(y_true, y_pred):
    return float(np.mean((np.asarray(y_true).squeeze() - np.asarray(y_pred).squeeze()) ** 2) ** 0.5)


def predictive_log_likelihood(Yt, y_true, tau):
    """Regression MC approximation of eq. (8) as coded in repo/net/net.py."""
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true).reshape(-1)
    ll = (logsumexp(-0.5 * tau * (y_true[None, :] - Yt) ** 2, axis=0)
          - np.log(Yt.shape[0]) - 0.5 * np.log(2 * np.pi) + 0.5 * np.log(tau))
    return float(np.mean(ll))


def evaluate(fit, X, y_true_raw, y_mean, y_std, tau, T=config.N_MC_SAMPLES):
    Yt = predictive_samples(fit, X, y_mean, y_std, T)
    mc_pred = Yt.mean(0)
    fit["model"].eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        std_pred = fit["model"](torch.as_tensor(X, dtype=torch.float32)).numpy().reshape(-1) * y_std + y_mean
    return {
        "mc_rmse": rmse(y_true_raw, mc_pred),
        "standard_rmse": rmse(y_true_raw, std_pred),
        "ll": predictive_log_likelihood(Yt, y_true_raw, tau),
    }


def grid_search(data, dropout_rates, tau_values, n_epochs, seed,
                batch_size=config.BATCH_SIZE, T=config.N_MC_SAMPLES, log=None):
    """Grid-search (dropout, tau) by validation predictive log-likelihood.

    Reproduces the loop in repo/experiment.py: every candidate is trained on the
    80% search portion and scored on the held-out 20% of the training rows.
    """
    s = data["search"]
    results = []
    best = None
    for gi, dropout in enumerate(dropout_rates):
        for ti, tau in enumerate(tau_values):
            fit_seed = seed * 1000 + gi * 100 + ti
            fit = train_model(s["X_tr"], s["y_tr"], dropout, tau, n_epochs, fit_seed,
                              batch_size=batch_size)
            ev = evaluate(fit, s["X_val"], s["y_val"], s["y_mean"], s["y_std"], tau, T=T)
            rec = {"dropout": float(dropout), "tau": float(tau), "val_ll": ev["ll"],
                   "val_mc_rmse": ev["mc_rmse"], "val_rmse": ev["standard_rmse"],
                   "reg": fit["reg"], "n_epochs": n_epochs, "seed": fit_seed}
            results.append(rec)
            if log is not None:
                log(rec)
            if best is None or rec["val_ll"] > best["val_ll"]:
                best = rec
    return best, results

"""Intermediate checks for the MC-dropout Boston Housing reproduction.

Run: python checks.py
These are the sanity checks listed in the plan; they validate data flow,
protocol bookkeeping and the weight-decay rule before the expensive run.
"""
import math
import os

import numpy as np

import config
import data_utils
import mc_dropout
from model import DropoutRegressor

FAILS = []


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    print("[{}] {} {}".format("ok" if ok else "FAIL", name, detail))
    if not ok:
        FAILS.append(name)


def main():
    ds = "bostonHousing"
    X, y, idxf, idxt = data_utils.load_raw(ds)
    check("data shape",
          X.shape == (506, 13) and y.shape == (506,) and len(idxf) == 13,
          "X{} y{} features{} target{}".format(X.shape, y.shape, len(idxf), idxt))

    ok_union = True
    for i in range(20):
        tr, te = data_utils.load_split_indices(ds, i)
        s_tr, s_te = set(tr.tolist()), set(te.tolist())
        ok_union &= (not (s_tr & s_te)) and len(s_tr | s_te) == 506 and max(s_tr | s_te) == 505
    check("splits disjoint / cover all rows", ok_union)

    rates, taus, base_epochs = data_utils.load_grid(ds)
    check("grid parsed", len(rates) == 4 and len(taus) == 3,
          "dropout={} tau={} base_epochs={}".format(rates, taus, base_epochs))

    m = DropoutRegressor(13, 50, p=0.05)
    check("parameter count 13*50+50+50+1", m.n_parameters() == 751, "{}".format(m.n_parameters()))

    # weight decay: reg = l^2 (1-p) / (2 N tau), monotone decreasing in tau
    n = 364
    regs = [mc_dropout.compute_reg(0.05, n, t) for t in [0.1, 0.15, 0.2]]
    hand = 1e-2 ** 2 * (1 - 0.05) / (2.0 * n * 0.1)
    check("weight decay matches hand computation", abs(regs[0] - hand) < 1e-18,
          "reg(tau=0.1)={:.6e}".format(regs[0]))
    check("weight decay decreases with tau", regs[0] > regs[1] > regs[2] > 0,
          "{:.3e} {:.3e} {:.3e}".format(*regs))

    # standardisation round trip + split hygiene
    d = data_utils.split_arrays(ds, 0)
    s, f = d["search"], d["final"]
    check("search/val sizes", s["X_tr"].shape[0] == 364 and s["X_val"].shape[0] == 91,
          "{}/{}".format(s["X_tr"].shape[0], s["X_val"].shape[0]))
    check("test size matches index file", f["X_test"].shape[0] == len(d["idx_test"]),
          "{}/{}".format(f["X_test"].shape[0], len(d["idx_test"])))
    ytr = s["y_tr"] * s["y_std"] + s["y_mean"]
    check("target standardisation is invertible",
          np.allclose(ytr, data_utils.load_raw(ds)[1][d["idx_train"]][:364], atol=1e-6))
    check("standardised train target ~ N(0,1)",
          abs(s["y_tr"].mean()) < 1e-6 and abs(s["y_tr"].std() - 1) < 1e-6,
          "mean {:.2e} std {:.6f}".format(s["y_tr"].mean(), s["y_tr"].std()))

    # a plain least-squares linear model on split 0: is the pipeline non-degenerate?
    from numpy.linalg import lstsq
    Xtr = np.hstack([s["X_tr"], np.ones((s["X_tr"].shape[0], 1))])
    w = lstsq(Xtr, s["y_tr"], rcond=None)[0]
    Xte = np.hstack([f["X_test"], np.ones((f["X_test"].shape[0], 1))])
    lin_pred = (Xte @ w) * f["y_std"] + f["y_mean"]
    lin_rmse = mc_dropout.rmse(d["y_test_raw"], lin_pred)
    check("linear baseline RMSE plausible", 2.0 < lin_rmse < 6.0, "linear RMSE {:.3f}".format(lin_rmse))

    # shortest real fit to time the budget (2 epochs, 1 grid point)
    import time
    t0 = time.time()
    fit = mc_dropout.train_model(s["X_tr"], s["y_tr"], 0.05, 0.1, 2, 11)
    ev = mc_dropout.evaluate(fit, s["X_val"], d["y_val_raw"], s["y_mean"], s["y_std"], 0.1, T=100)
    dt = time.time() - t0
    check("short fit finite", np.isfinite(ev["mc_rmse"]) and np.isfinite(ev["ll"]),
          "val MC RMSE {:.3f} LL {:+.3f} in {:.2f}s (2 epochs + 100 MC)".format(
              ev["mc_rmse"], ev["ll"], dt))
    print("Estimated cost: {:.2f}s per 2 epochs + 100 MC -> 400 epochs ~ {:.1f}s per fit".format(
        dt, dt * 200))

    anchor = None
    p = os.path.join(config.results_dir(ds), "test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt")
    if os.path.exists(p):
        vals = np.loadtxt(p)
        anchor = (float(vals.mean()), float(vals.std() / math.sqrt(len(vals))))
        check("authors' released anchor readable", True,
              "released 100x-epoch MC RMSE {:.4f} +- {:.4f} over {} splits".format(*anchor, len(vals)))

    print()
    if FAILS:
        print("FAILED: {}".format(FAILS))
        return 1
    print("all checks passed")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""PyTorch port of the authors' dropout regression network (repo/net/net.py).

Architecture (repo/net/net.py with 1 hidden layer):

    Dropout(p_in) -> Dense(n_hidden, relu) -> Dropout(p_out) -> Dense(1)

i.e. dropout before *every* weight layer (R2).  `p_in` is the input-to-hidden
rate and `p_out` the hidden-to-output rate; the paper states two rates (0.05 and
0.005, A2) and the authors' released code instead grid-searches a single rate
used at both places -- both layouts are supported here.

L2 regularisation follows eq. (7) of the paper / net.py:
``reg = lengthscale**2 * (1 - p) / (2 * N * tau)`` applied to each layer's
kernel with that layer's own dropout probability (R3).

Dropout stays active at prediction time for MC sampling (net.py calls the
network with ``training=True``), which is what this module implements through
`DropoutRegressor.sample_mode`.
"""
import os

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# tiny networks: multi-threading only adds overhead; workers set this to 1
torch.set_num_threads(max(1, min(4, (os.cpu_count() or 2))))


class DropoutRegressor(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_in, n_hidden=50, p_in=0.05, p_out=0.005, seed=None):
        super().__init__()
        if seed is not None:
            torch.manual_seed(seed)
        self.drop_in = nn.Dropout(p_in)
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(n_in, n_hidden)
        self.drop_out = nn.Dropout(p_out)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(n_hidden, 1)
        self.reset_parameters()

    def reset_parameters(self):
        # Keras Dense defaults: glorot_uniform kernels, zero biases
        nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.fc1.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.fc1.bias)
        nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.fc2.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.fc2.bias)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.drop_in(x)
        x = torch.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = self.drop_out(x)
        return self.fc2(x)

    def n_parameters(self):
        return sum(p.numel() for p in self.parameters())

    def sample_mode(self, on):
        """`on=True` keeps dropout active with no gradient tracking (net.py's
        training=True at prediction time); `on=False` is the deterministic net."""
        if on:
            self.eval()
            for m in self.modules():
                if isinstance(m, nn.Dropout):
                    m.train()
        else:
            self.eval()


def mc_forward(model, X, T, chunk=200000, seed=None):
    """T stochastic forward passes with dropout on; returns (mean, var).

    Mirrors net.py's mc_predict: each row's samples share the *same* dropout
    masks (Keras applies one mask per batch row), so the samples are indexed
    [sample, row].
    """
    n = X.shape[0]
    model.sample_mode(True)
    means = []
    varis = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        done = 0
        while done < T:
            k = min(T - done, max(1, chunk // n))
            xr = X.repeat(k, 1)
            out = model(xr).reshape(k, n)
            means.append(out.mean(dim=0))
            varis.append(out.var(dim=0, unbiased=True))
            done += k
    mean = torch.cat(means).mean(dim=0)
    var = torch.cat(varis).mean(dim=0)
    model.sample_mode(False)
    return mean, var


def to_tensor(a):
    return torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(a, dtype=np.float32))


def forward_gaussian(model, X):
    """Deterministic forward pass -> Gaussian likelihood (net.py's predict)."""
    model.sample_mode(False)
    with torch.no_grad():
        return model(to_tensor(X))

"""Training / MC-dropout evaluation core (port of repo/net/net.py).

One "fit" = one (p_in, p_out, tau) triplet trained for a fixed number of epochs
(no early stopping, R12) with Adam (R6) on the mean squared error plus the eq.(7)
weight decay (R3).  Evaluation = MC dropout (R8) giving predictive mean/variance
and the regression log-likelihood of eq. (8) (R9).
"""
import numpy as np
import torch
from scipy.special import logsumexp

import config
from model import DropoutRegressor, mc_forward, to_tensor


def compute_reg(p, n_train, tau, lengthscale=None):
    """Weight-decay factor from repo/net/net.py:

        reg = lengthscale**2 * (1 - dropout) / (2. * N * tau)

    (the paper's eq. (7) relation between l, tau and the L2 penalty; R3/A7).
    """
    if lengthscale is None:
        lengthscale = config.PRIOR_LENGTHSCALE
    return lengthscale ** 2 * (1.0 - p) / (2.0 * n_train * tau)


def reg_factors(hyp, n_train):
    return [compute_reg(hyp["p_in"], n_train, hyp["tau"]),
            compute_reg(hyp["p_out"], n_train, hyp["tau"])]


def train_model(X_tr, y_tr, hyp, n_epochs, seed, batch_size=None,
                lr=None, shuffle=True):
    """Train one dropout net for a fixed number of epochs (R5, R12).

    Loss = MSE (+ implicit l2_loss(0) term of net.py) + reg * ||kernel||^2 per
    Dense layer, exactly the objective of net.py's `model.compile`.
    """
    if batch_size is None:
        batch_size = config.BATCH_SIZE
    if lr is None:
        lr = config.ADAM_LR
    n = X_tr.shape[0]
    regs = reg_factors(hyp, n)

    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    model = DropoutRegressor(X_tr.shape[1], config.N_HIDDEN_UNITS,
                             p_in=hyp["p_in"], p_out=hyp["p_out"], seed=seed)
    optim = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)   # Keras 2.2 defaults (A6)
    x = to_tensor(X_tr)
    y = to_tensor(y_tr)
    mse = torch.nn.MSELoss()

    for _ in range(int(n_epochs)):
        perm = torch.randperm(n) if shuffle else torch.arange(n)
        for s in range(0, n, batch_size):
            idx = perm[s:s + batch_size]
            optim.zero_grad()
            out = model(x[idx]).squeeze(-1)
            loss = mse(out, y[idx])
            loss = loss + regs[0] * model.fc1.weight.pow(2).sum() \
                        + regs[1] * model.fc2.weight.pow(2).sum()
            loss.backward()
            optim.step()
    model.sample_mode(False)
    return model


def mc_predict(model, X, T=None, seed=None):
    if T is None:
        T = config.N_MC_SAMPLES
    if seed is not None:
        torch.manual_seed(seed)
    return mc_forward(model, to_tensor(X), T=T)


def rmse(y_true_raw, y_pred_raw):
    d = np.asarray(y_true_raw, dtype=np.float64) - np.asarray(y_pred_raw, dtype=np.float64)
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(d ** 2)))


def predictive_log_likelihood(y, mean, var, tau):
    """eq. (8) / net.py's mc_predict: a mixture of T Gaussians with the
    observation precision tau, evaluated with logsumexp."""
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
    mean = np.asarray(mean, dtype=np.float64)
    var = np.asarray(var, dtype=np.float64)
    ll = -0.5 * np.log(2 * np.pi) - 0.5 * np.log(tau) - 0.5 * tau * (y - mean) ** 2 \
         - 0.5 * tau * var
    return float(np.mean(logsumexp(ll, b=1.0 / var.shape[0]) - np.log(var.shape[0])))


def evaluate(model, X, y_raw, y_mean, y_std, tau, T=None, seed=None):
    """MC-dropout evaluation on raw-target units.

    `y_raw` are target values in the original units; MC predictions are
    inverse-standardised with the (train) target statistics.
    """
    m, v = mc_predict(model, X, T=T, seed=seed)
    mean_std = m.numpy().astype(np.float64)
    var_std = v.numpy().astype(np.float64)
    mean_raw = mean_std * y_std + y_mean                    # A13: original units
    ll_std = predictive_log_likelihood(
        (np.asarray(y_raw, dtype=np.float64) - y_mean) / y_std, mean_std, var_std, tau)
    ll_raw = ll_std - np.log(y_std)                          # change of variables
    return {"mc_rmse": rmse(y_raw, mean_raw),
            "ll": ll_raw,
            "ll_standardised": ll_std,
            "preds": mean_raw}


def grid_search(data, hyp_space, n_epochs, seed, batch_size=None, T=None, log=print):
    """Score every candidate (p_in, p_out, tau) by validation log-likelihood.

    Returns (best_hyp, records) -- the selection rule of the authors' released
    code, which replaces the paper's 40-iteration Spearmint BO (R4/A15).
    """
    s = data["search"]
    recs = []
    for gi, cand in enumerate(hyp_space):
        hyp = dict(cand)
        model = train_model(s["X_tr"], s["y_tr"], hyp, n_epochs,
                            seed * 1000 + gi, batch_size=batch_size)
        ev = evaluate(model, s["X_val"], data["y_val_raw"], s["y_mean"], s["y_std"],
                      hyp["tau"], T=T, seed=seed * 1000 + gi + 500000)
        rec = dict(hyp)
        rec.update({"val_ll": ev["ll"], "val_mc_rmse": ev["mc_rmse"],
                    "reg_in": compute_reg(hyp["p_in"], s["X_tr"].shape[0], hyp["tau"]),
                    "reg_out": compute_reg(hyp["p_out"], s["X_tr"].shape[0], hyp["tau"])})
        recs.append(rec)
        log("    grid p_in={g[p_in]:.3f} p_out={g[p_out]:.3f} tau={g[tau]:g} -> val LL {v:+.4f} "
            "(val MC RMSE {r:.4f}, reg {gin:.3e}/{gout:.3e})".format(
                g=rec, v=rec["val_ll"], r=rec["val_mc_rmse"],
                gin=rec["reg_in"], gout=rec["reg_out"]))
    best = max(recs, key=lambda r: r["val_ll"])
    best_hyp = {k: best[k] for k in ("p_in", "p_out", "tau")}
    return best_hyp, recs

"""Reproduce the MC-dropout UCI regression result (paper Table 1, Boston Housing).

Single entrypoint.  Protocol (digested from the authors' released code,
repo/experiment.py + repo/net/net.py, which is the apparatus that produced the
paper numbers):

  for each released train/test split i (index_train_i.txt / index_test_i.txt):
    1. carve the LAST 20% of the training rows off as a validation set
       (num_training_examples = int(0.8 * n_train), no shuffling)
    2. grid-search the hyperparameters (dropout rate, tau) by *validation*
       predictive log-likelihood, each candidate trained on the 80% search rows
       (net.py's weight decay reg = l^2 (1-p) / (2 N tau), paper eq. 7)
    3. retrain from scratch on ALL training rows with the winning pair, for a
       fixed number of epochs (40 * epoch multiplier, no early stopping)
    4. MC dropout on the released test rows: T stochastic forward passes with
       dropout active -> test RMSE in original target units + predictive log
       likelihood (net.py's logsumexp mixture form of paper eq. 8)

Usage
  python reproduce.py                     # Boston Housing, 20 splits, 400 epochs (Table 1 / C1)
  python reproduce.py --smoke             # tiny end-to-end check
  python reproduce.py --dataset concrete --split-count 20
  python reproduce.py --epochx 100        # Table 2 setting (4000 epochs)
  python reproduce.py --dropout-mode paper  # A2 layout: p_in=0.05, p_out=0.005
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import re
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor

import numpy as np

import config
import data_utils
import mc_dropout

RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(config.WORKSPACE, "results")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def hyp_space(mode, dataset):
    """Candidate (p_in, p_out, tau) triples + the dataset's base epoch count.

    'grid'  : authors' released code -- one dropout rate used at every dropout
              layer, grid-searched together with tau (dropout_rates.txt x
              tau_values.txt).
    'paper' : paper text / A2 -- p_in=0.05 (input->hidden), p_out=0.005
              (hidden->output), fixed; only tau is searched (grid stands in for
              the paper's 40-iteration Spearmint BO, R4).
    """
    rates, taus, base_epochs = data_utils.load_grid(dataset)
    if mode == "grid":
        cands = [dict(p_in=r, p_out=r, tau=t) for r in rates for t in taus]
    elif mode == "paper":
        cands = [dict(p_in=config.DROPOUT_PROB_IN, p_out=config.DROPOUT_PROB_OUT, tau=t)
                 for t in taus]
    else:
        raise ValueError("unknown dropout mode " + mode)
    return cands, base_epochs


def _released_file(dataset, kind, epochx, hidden=1):
    return os.path.join(config.results_dir(dataset),
                        "{}_{}_xepochs_{}_hidden_layers.txt".format(kind, epochx, hidden))


def released_per_split(dataset, kind, epochx=100, hidden=1):
    p = _released_file(dataset, kind, epochx, hidden)
    if not os.path.exists(p):
        return None
    return np.loadtxt(p).astype(float).ravel()


def released_selection(dataset, epochx=100, hidden=1):
    """Recover the authors' selected (dropout rate, tau) per split.

    Their released validation-LL file has 12 lines per split, in the loop order
    of experiment.py (dropout rate outer, tau inner); the selected pair is the
    argmax of that block.  Verified to agree with their released test_tau file.
    """
    p = _released_file(dataset, "validation_ll", epochx, hidden)
    if not os.path.exists(p):
        return None
    recs = []
    for ln in open(p).read().strip().split("\n"):
        head, val = ln.split("::")
        m = re.search(r"Dropout_Rate: (\S+) Tau: (\S+)", head)
        recs.append((float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(2)), float(val)))
    rates, taus, _ = data_utils.load_grid(dataset)
    per_split = len(rates) * len(taus)
    sel = []
    for i in range(len(recs) // per_split):
        block = recs[i * per_split:(i + 1) * per_split]
        d, t, _ = max(block, key=lambda r: r[2])
        sel.append(dict(p_in=d, p_out=d, tau=t))
    return sel


# ------------------------------------------------------------------- one split
def run_split(task):
    """Train + evaluate one split (executed in a worker process)."""
    import torch
    torch.set_num_threads(1)                     # workers are parallel at split level
    dataset = task["dataset"]
    split = task["split"]
    t0 = time.time()
    data = data_utils.split_arrays(dataset, split)
    cands, base_epochs = hyp_space(task["mode"], dataset)
    n_epochs = int(base_epochs * task["epochx"])
    s, f = data["search"], data["final"]
    log_lines = []

    if task.get("fixed_hyp") is not None:
        hyp = dict(task["fixed_hyp"])
        grid_records = []
    else:
        hyp, grid_records = mc_dropout.grid_search(
            data, cands, n_epochs, config.SEED + split, batch_size=task["batch_size"],
            T=task["T"], log=log_lines.append)
        for ln in log_lines:
            print(ln, flush=True)

    t_fit0 = time.time()
    model = mc_dropout.train_model(f["X_tr"], f["y_tr"], hyp, n_epochs,
                                   config.SEED + 7919 * (split + 1),
                                   batch_size=task["batch_size"])
    ev = mc_dropout.evaluate(model, f["X_test"], data["y_test_raw"], f["y_mean"], f["y_std"],
                             hyp["tau"], T=task["T"])
    rec = dict(split=split, mode=task["mode"], n_epochs=n_epochs, n_params=model.n_parameters(),

               test_mc_rmse=ev["mc_rmse"], test_ll=ev["ll"],
               test_mc_std=ev["pred_std"], n_test=int(f["X_test"].shape[0]),
